Subject: Clarify billing for cross-session KV reuse & rounding

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency and token-cost numbers looked promising. Before we proceed to PO, procurement has two specific billing questions that would impact our forecast and approval:

1) KV / prefix cache reuse: our product issues a LOT of short bursts (30-120 tokens) but with long-lived session affinity—clients reconnect to different hosts at times. If a host has to rehydrate the KV cache for the same conversation, will Redwood bill those cached tokens again? In other words, is cache rehydration treated as billed input tokens each time, or do you have a mechanism to avoid double-billing across rehydrates?

2) Rounding / minimums for streaming vs non-streaming: how do you round charges for streaming endpoints (we stream partial tokens back to the client) vs the non-streaming generate endpoint? We have scenarios where requests are 8-40 tokens but happen constantly; rounding rules change our monthly estimate materially.

Can you give a clear example (two scenarios) showing how a 35-token request with a 120-token cached prefix gets billed under your current hosted pricing model? Also share any concessions available for early customers that would ensure we don't get double-billed while testing in production.

Procurement has asked that we get this in writing (simple examples + any line-item wording they can include on the PO).

Thanks — Jill

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Clarify billing for cross-session KV reuse & rounding

Hi Jill — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise explanation plus two worked examples and a proposed short-term concession for Streamlytics while you ramp.

Short answers up front:
- Cache rehydration: by default Redwood bills the tokens that are actually sent to the model (input + output). Cached KV tokens are NOT billed on every request if the host can serve requests from an in-memory KV cache. However, when a request is routed to a host that does not have the cache (a rehydrate), the host must rehydrate the KV prefix from persistent storage and we count the tokens used to reconstruct the KV in the model prompt for that request.
- Rounding: for the hosted streaming endpoints we round billed token usage up to the nearest 25-token bucket per request, with a configurable monthly floor for new customers. For non-streaming (batch/generate) we round to the nearest 10-token bucket.

Important operational detail: we attempt session affinity for 15 minutes by default and have a 60-minute soft TTL on the in-memory KV. If your client reconnects to a different host after the TTL or outside affinity, you may see a one-time rehydration cost. Over steady state, rehydrations typically drop to <1% of requests for long-lived conversations.

Worked examples (hosted API, standard config):
A) Short burst, cache available
- Client request: 35 tokens (new content)
- Cached prefix: 120 tokens (already in memory on the serving host)
- Billed tokens: 35 (input) + output tokens (e.g., 45) = 80 tokens -> rounding up to nearest 25 -> billed as 100 tokens

B) Short burst, rehydration occurred (different host)
- Client request: 35 tokens (new content)
- Cached prefix needs rehydration: 120 tokens re-streamed into model prompt for reconstruction
- Billed tokens: 120 (rehydration) + 35 (new input) + 45 (output) = 200 tokens -> rounding up to nearest 25 -> billed as 200 tokens

Note the delta is the one-time rehydration amount (roughly 120 tokens) when a host misses the in-memory cache.

Monthly estimate advice:
- If you have many short bursts with stable session affinity, use the steady-state math (example A) and model rehydrations as a small % of total requests.
- If you expect frequent reconnects across hosts (e.g., mobile users with short sessions), add a conservative rehydration factor (we suggest 3-8% of requests for planning) multiplied by your average cached prefix size.

Proposed concession for Streamlytics (pilot / first 3 months):
- We will: 
  * Apply a "KV-rehydration credit" that refunds up to 80% of the first 300k tokens that look like rehydration on the monthly invoice during the 3-month pilot.
  * Use actual-token billing for your account (no 25-token rounding) for the pilot where usage < 50k tokens/month. Above that threshold, standard rounding applies.

Attachments: rate_card_v3.pdf — includes the line-item name we recommend you reference on the PO: "Redwood hosted inference - token usage (per-token, post-credits)".

If that sounds acceptable I can put the concession language into a short term sheet and loop legal/finance to finalize.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: concession math + invoice line items for DL-4721

Stephanie / Marissa — quick alignment before I share the term sheet with Jill:

Proposal (finalized numbers):
- Pilot duration: 3 months; applies to hosted API only.
- KV-rehydration credit: refund 80% of tokens flagged as "rehydration" up to 300,000 tokens per month. Flagging algorithm = tokens with identical prefix hash seen in <24 hours but billed on requests that originate from different host_ids.
- Rounding during pilot: actual-token accounting for months where total usage < 50k tokens; otherwise round to 25-token buckets.
- Floor: no monthly floor for the pilot; after pilot default floor = 15,000 tokens/month unless overridden by enterprise contract.

Draft invoice line items (to include in PO wording):
1) Redwood hosted inference - token usage (post-credits): line-item shows raw billed tokens and credits as separate rows.
2) KV-rehydration credit (DL-4721 pilot): description + credit line for the month.
3) Reserved support: optional, if they want 24/7 SLA.

Please OK and I will push term sheet + DocuSign. If legal needs the exact flagging algorithm text I can include the pseudocode as an appendix.
- Karthik
